title: Subject Pronouns: jeg, du, han, hun, vi, dere, de
goal: Choose and use Bokmål subject pronouns in simple sentences.

objectives.statement: Choose and use Bokmål subject pronouns in simple sentences.

spans.value: Maja has arrived for her first morning as a volunteer at a small community café. Jonas introduces the other volunteers and helps organize the work.
Hei, jeg heter Maja. Er du Jonas?

blocks.translation: Hi, my name is Maja. Are you Jonas?

spans.value: Ja, jeg er Jonas. Hun der er Sara, og han heter Emil.

blocks.translation: Yes, I’m Jonas. That woman over there is Sara, and his name is Emil.

spans.value: Ja, de jobber på kafeen. Vi begynner klokka ni.

blocks.translation: Yes, they work at the café. We start at nine.

spans.value: Emil, du lager kaffe. Maja og Jonas, dere setter stolene her.

blocks.translation: Emil, you make coffee. Maja and Jonas, you put the chairs here.

spans.value: Jeg baker. Vi åpner klokka ti.

blocks.translation: I’m baking. We open at ten.
Are Nora and Ali coming too?

spans.value: The volunteers repeatedly use short words such as
instead of repeating names. To understand each sentence, you need to know who is speaking, who is being addressed, and who is being discussed.

sections.title: Replacing a name with a subject pronoun

spans.value: is a short word that identifies the person or people a sentence is about. It normally comes before the verb in the simple sentences used here.
because she is speaking about herself.
because Emil is one male person already known from the context.
Norwegian has seven subject pronouns in this lesson:

items.value: — he — one male person being discussed
— she — one female person being discussed
— we — the speaker and one or more other people
— you — two or more people being addressed
— they — two or more people being discussed

spans.value: The central question is not simply “How many people are there?” You must also ask what relationship those people have to the conversation: Are they speaking, being addressed, or being discussed?
when the speaker includes at least one other person.
In the first sentence, the speaker refers only to themself. In the second, the speaker includes other people.

Common mistake: using vi for any group
does not mean every group of several people. It means a group that includes the speaker.

spans.value: when speaking directly to one person.

spans.value: for both one person and several people. Bokmål makes the difference explicit:

no.value: Emil og Maja, dere lager kaffe.

The chairs are now in place, and Nora and Ali arrive.
Hei! Jeg heter Nora, og han heter Ali.

blocks.translation: Hi! My name is Nora, and his name is Ali.

spans.value: Ja, jeg jobber her i dag. Sara og jeg baker. Vi er snart ferdige.

blocks.translation: Yes, I’m working here today. Sara and I are baking. We’ll soon be finished.

spans.value: Nora og Ali, dere kan sette koppene på bordet.

blocks.translation: Nora and Ali, you can put the cups on the table.

The next day, four classmates meet at the library to prepare a class display. The setting has changed, but the same perspective choices still apply.

One student introduces herself and another student. A classmate asks one person whether that person is ready. Someone gives an instruction to two classmates together. Later, one student reports what those two classmates are doing. Finally, the speaker describes a task shared with another person.

Without looking back, write the Bokmål subject pronoun for each meaning: the speaker alone, one listener, one male person discussed, one female person discussed, the speaker with others, several listeners, and several people discussed. Then write three simple sentences: one with
. Your sentences should make clear who is included, addressed, or discussed.

prompt.value: Read the three café lines and choose the complete reference mapping. The goal is to identify who each pronoun represents, not to translate. Maja: «Ja, jeg jobber her i dag.» (Yes, I work here today.) Ali: «Jobber du her, Maja?» (Do you work here, Maja?) Emil, about Nora and Ali: «De er raske!» (They are quick!) Which mapping is correct for jeg, du, and de?

options.text: Maja bruker «jeg» om seg selv (I); Ali bruker «du» til Nora og Ali (you, two or more people); Emil bruker «de» om Maja (they).
options.why: Ali addresses Maja alone, and Emil discusses Nora and Ali.

prompt.value: At a library table, write five short, simple Bokmål sentences for these exchanges. Use subject pronouns according to each perspective and use the library situation rather than the café wording: 1. Nora introduces herself and refers to Ali as another student. 2. Maja asks Ali, one person, whether he is ready. 3. Jonas tells Nora and Ali together to put the books on the table. 4. Maja tells Jonas what Nora and Ali are doing; she is talking about them, not to them. 5. Nora describes a task she shares with Ali. Write only the five Norwegian sentences.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Accept natural Bokmål variants that preserve the required conversational role and subject-pronoun reference; do not require exact vocabulary beyond the requested library situation.

criteria.instruction: Uses *jeg* for Nora as speaker and *han* for Ali as the male person being discussed in the introduction.
Uses *du* when Maja addresses Ali, one person, in the readiness question.
Uses *dere* when Jonas addresses Nora and Ali together.
Uses *de* when Maja discusses Nora and Ali with Jonas.
Uses *vi* when Nora describes a task shared with Ali.
